description: Single-frame fleet explorer: Fleet → Super Unit → Rack → Tray → GPU. Click a tile to descend, click a breadcrumb to come back up; the whole drill-down happens on this dashboard. Colour is health, never utilisation. Live metrics only.

options.content:
Live Topology Fleet ▸ $su ▸ $rack ▸ $node
Click a tile to descend a level · click a crumb (or the SU / Rack / Tray pickers above) to come back up · everything stays on this page. Colour is health, never utilisation — an idle GPU at 0 % is green. Live sources only: up, node_*, DCGM_FI_DEV_*, cgroup_info (Slurm) and Loki.

panels.title: ① Fleet — live inventory (all 7 Super Units)

panels.description: GB300 trays whose node-exporter reported at least once in the last 15 minutes. Windowed on purpose: an instant count of `up` flaps with the scrape cycle and misreports whole SUs as dead. Per-SU breakdown in the Super-Unit rollup table below.
panels.title: Trays reporting

panels.description: Racks with at least one reporting tray in the last 15 minutes. The per-rack tiles in section ③ name every one of them.
panels.title: Racks reporting

panels.description: GB300 GPUs currently exporting DCGM telemetry (4 per tray).
panels.title: GPUs reporting (DCGM)

panels.description: Highest GPU core temperature anywhere in the fleet right now. Per-SU maxima in the rollup table below; per-GPU values in section ⑤.
panels.title: Hottest GPU now

panels.description: Sum of DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE across every reporting GPU. GPU power only — host/board power is node_hwmon_power_average_watt and is counted separately. Trend by SU at the bottom of the board.
panels.title: Fleet GPU power

panels.description: GPUs that raised at least one XID in the last 24 hours. DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS is a sparse metric — it only exists while an XID is latched, so it is always read with max_over_time(...[24h]). Every GPU counted here is listed by name in the fault table at the bottom.
panels.title: GPUs with an XID (24 h)
② Super Units — click a tile to blow the SU open into its racks

panels.description: Tray availability: trays reporting in the last 15 min as a percentage of the trays this Super Unit has had online in the last 24 h. Self-normalising, so no nameplate is assumed. Red = a real outage — SU6 is at ~5 % because it is under vendor NVSwitch maintenance. Raw counts in the table directly below.
panels.title: $su_all

panels.description: One row per Super Unit, same selectors as the tiles above: 'Trays now' summed over the 7 rows equals the fleet 'Trays reporting' tile, and 'Tray availability' is exactly the number printed on each SU tile.
panels.title: Super-Unit rollup — the 7 tiles above, by name and by number
③ Racks in $su — click a rack to blow it open into its trays

panels.description: Trays reporting in this rack in the last 15 minutes. A full GB300 rack is 18 trays: green only at 18/18, amber 15-17, red below 15. A rack showing 0 has no tray reporting at all — the whole rack is dark, not idle.
panels.title: $rack_all
④ Trays in $rack — click a tray to blow it open into its GPUs

panels.description: Tray health = the WORST of its four exporters (node-exporter, DCGM, cgroup-exporter, Alloy). Green only when all four are up. 'NO DATA' means the tray produced no series at all in the dashboard window — it is dark, not idle. Uptime, load, temperature and per-exporter state are in the table below.
panels.title: $node_all

panels.description: One row per tray in $rack — the entities behind the tiles above. Row count equals the rack tile's number. This is the detail the tray tiles cannot show: uptime, each exporter separately, host CPU load, GPU and chassis temperature, GPU utilisation and GPU power.
panels.title: Tray detail — $rack · uptime · exporters · CPU load · temperature · GPU util · power
⑤ GPUs on $node — red / green is health, not utilisation

panels.description:
Per-GPU health score, deliberately NOT utilisation — an idle GPU reads 0 % and stays green.
FAULT (red): GPU core ≥ 88 °C, or an uncorrectable (DBE) ECC error, or a row-remap failure.
WARNING (amber): GPU core ≥ 80 °C, or an XID raised in the last 24 h.
HEALTHY (green): none of the above. Every input is in the table below.

targets.expr: clamp_max( max by (gpu)(   2 * (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP{node="$node", gpu="$gpu_all"} >= bool 88) + 2 * (DCGM_FI_DEV_ECC_DBE_VOL_TOTAL{node="$node", gpu="$gpu_all"} > bool 0) + 2 * (DCGM_FI_DEV_ROW_REMAP_FAILURE{node="$node", gpu="$gpu_all"} > bool 0) + 1 * (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP{node="$node", gpu="$gpu_all"} >= bool 80)) + 1 * clamp_max((count by (gpu)(max_over_time(DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS{node="$node", gpu="$gpu_all"}[24h])) or (max by (gpu)(DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP{node="$node", gpu="$gpu_all"}) * 0)), 1), 2)

panels.title: GPU $gpu_all

panels.description: Every input to the GPU tiles above, per GPU on $node. 'Worst XID 24 h' is the highest XID code seen in 24 h (0 = none recorded); DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS is sparse so it is always read with max_over_time. Utilisation is shown in blue because it is information, not health.
panels.title: GPU detail — $node · util · temperature · power · clocks · memory · ECC · XID
⑥ Operations — Slurm · GPU faults · thermals · power · tray logs

panels.description:
Live Slurm allocation, read from the slurmstepd cgroups the trays export (cgroup_info{jobid,username}), windowed over 15 minutes because the metric is scraped per tray. One row per job per Super Unit; the value is the number of DISTINCT trays that job holds. There is no slurm-exporter on this cluster — this is the real allocation signal, not a stand-in.
Every tray carries two cgroups per job — the stepd's own (uid 0) and the job owner's — so uid 0 is filtered out and trays are de-duplicated per job before counting. Without that the total over-reports by ~25 %.

targets.expr: count by (jobid, username, su)(count by (jobid, username, su, node)(max_over_time(cgroup_info{uid!="0", username!=""}[15m])))

panels.title: Slurm — trays allocated per job right now

panels.description: One row per (tray, GPU, XID code) seen in the last 24 hours — the exact GPUs behind the 'GPUs with an XID (24 h)' tile at the top. Fleet-wide on purpose: faults must be visible without first drilling to the rack.
panels.title: GPU faults — every XID raised in the last 24 h

panels.description: sum by (su)(DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE) over the dashboard window. The sum of the last points equals the 'Fleet GPU power' tile at the top. GPU power only; host/board rails are node_hwmon_power_average_watt.
panels.title: Power — GPU power draw by Super Unit

panels.description: max by (su)(DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP) plus max(node_thermal_zone_temp), the ACPI chassis zone every tray exports — the only live cooling signal on this fleet (the BMC/Redfish and facility BMS exporters are stopped, so nothing here is sourced from them).
panels.title: Thermals & cooling — hottest GPU per Super Unit, and hottest tray chassis

panels.description: Live Loki streams for the selected tray. job="kernel" carries no per-tray streams on this fleet, so the panel reads the streams that do exist: syslog, dmesg, journal and slurm.
panels.title: Tray logs — $node · kernel, syslog, journal and Slurm
